messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi, I’m having trouble sending MMS messages with my messaging app. It’s been happening for the past few hours, and I’m currently in France. Can you help me fix this?

To assist you with your MMS issue, I’ll need to identify your account first. Could you please provide either:

- The phone number associated with your account, or
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format)?

This will help me check your line and data settings to resolve the problem.
Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002 and my name is John Smith. Let me know if you need any more details.

Thank you for the details. I see that your line is currently not set up for international roaming, which is required for MMS and mobile data to work while you are in France. I have now enabled roaming on your line.

Please try sending an MMS again. If it still doesn’t work, let me know and I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried, but I’m still unable to send MMS messages. What should I do next?

Let’s continue troubleshooting. To help identify the issue, please check if you can use mobile data (for example, browsing the web) while in France. Also, could you let me know if you see any error messages when trying to send an MMS, or does it just fail to send?

Next, I’ll guide you through a quick check on your phone:

1. Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
   - Do you see any signal bars?
   - Is there a “4G”, “5G”, or similar icon?
   - Is Airplane Mode enabled?
   - Do you see a “Data” or “Mobile Data” icon?

This information will help me determine if your phone is connected to the network and if mobile data is active.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see that Airplane Mode is enabled. I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?

Airplane Mode disables all wireless connections, including cellular service and mobile data, which are required for sending MMS messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once it is off, wait a few seconds for your phone to reconnect to the network. Then, check if you see signal bars and a mobile data icon (such as “4G” or “5G”) in your status bar.

After doing this, try sending an MMS message again and let me know if it works or if you encounter any issues.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, my status bar shows “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” I still don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?

Since your phone is showing “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” let’s try to restore your connection step by step.

First, please try the following:
1. Make sure your SIM card is properly inserted. If you know how, you can remove and reinsert your SIM card, or let me know if you need instructions.
2. After reseating the SIM card, check if you now see any signal bars or if the “No Signal” message disappears.

Let me know if you’re able to do this, or if you need guidance on how to reseat your SIM card. Once done, please update me on what you see in your status bar.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve reinserted my SIM card. Now, my status bar shows a weak signal (poor), “2G,” and “Data Disabled.” What should I do next?

Your phone is now detecting the SIM card and connecting to the network, but it’s on a 2G connection and mobile data is still disabled. MMS requires at least a 3G connection and mobile data to be enabled.

Let’s do the following steps:

1. Change your network mode to prefer 4G/5G (if available) to improve your connection.
2. Enable mobile data on your phone.

Please update your network mode to “4G/5G Preferred” in your phone’s settings. After that, turn on mobile data. Once you’ve done both, let me know what your status bar shows (signal strength, network type, and if data is enabled). If you need instructions for either step, let me know!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve set my network mode to “4G/5G Preferred” and turned on mobile data. Now, my status bar shows excellent signal strength, “5G,” and data is enabled. What should I do next?

Great! Your phone now has excellent signal strength, is connected to 5G, and mobile data is enabled. Please try sending an MMS message again.

If the MMS still does not send, let me know if you receive any error messages or if it simply fails to send. If it works, please confirm so I know your issue is resolved.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I tried sending an MMS again, but it still won’t go through. There’s no specific error message—it just fails to send. What should I try next?

Let’s check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN or missing MMSC URL can prevent MMS from working.

Please check your APN settings on your phone and let me know if you see an MMSC URL listed. If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings to default, which often resolves MMS issues.

Would you like instructions to reset your APN settings? After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect. Let me know how you’d like to proceed.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and the APN name is set to “internet” with the MMSC URL as “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Should I still reset the APN settings to default and reboot my device, or is there something else I should try first?

Your APN settings appear correct, including the MMSC URL, which is essential for MMS. Since your network and data are working, and your APN settings look good, let’s check one more thing that can affect MMS: Wi-Fi Calling.

Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your device? If so, please try turning it off and then attempt to send an MMS again. Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS delivery, especially when roaming internationally.

Let me know if Wi-Fi Calling is on, and if turning it off helps. If MMS still doesn’t work after this, we can proceed with resetting your APN settings and rebooting your device as the next step.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently enabled on my device. Should I go ahead and turn it off now and then try sending an MMS again?

Yes, please turn off Wi-Fi Calling on your device. After turning it off, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the mobile network, then try sending an MMS message again.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still experience problems sending MMS. If it still doesn’t work, we’ll proceed with resetting your APN settings and rebooting your device.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.

Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending an MMS again, but it still won’t send. What should I do next?

Since turning off Wi-Fi Calling did not resolve the issue, the next step is to reset your APN settings to default and then reboot your device. This can often fix any hidden configuration issues that may be affecting MMS.

Please follow these steps:
1. Reset your APN settings to default on your device.
2. After resetting, reboot (restart) your device.

Once your device has restarted, try sending an MMS message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still encounter problems.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
